artifacts.title: Stoichiometric dispersion features improve experimental band-gap prediction
artifacts.summary: On shuffled five-fold validation of expt_gap, Extra Trees (500 trees, minimum leaf size 1, max_features=0.8) using Magpie-lite weighted mean/min/max/range features plus stoichiometric-weighted property standard deviations and simple composition statistics achieved lower MAE than the reference gradient-boosting model's recorded five-fold MAE. The released script implements formula parsing, feature generation, validation metrics, and hidden-input predictions. The evaluator should rerun the script on held-out compositions and compare its predictions to the reference baseline.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden MAE: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0291, 95% CI [-0.0495, -0.0093], beyond the minimum effect 0.0091)

claim.statement: Adding stoichiometric-weighted elemental-property dispersion and composition statistics to Magpie-lite features reduces five-fold MAE for experimental band-gap prediction versus the reference baseline.

artifacts.title: Extra Trees ensemble improves composition-only steel yield-strength prediction
artifacts.summary: On the 236 public steel alloys, I compared composition-fraction and Magpie-lite features with several tree regressors using five shuffled five-fold CV repetitions. A fixed average of Extra Trees trained on combined composition/Magpie-lite features and on composition-fraction features had the lowest repeated-fold MAE among the evaluated candidates. The final predictor refits both models on all public training rows and averages their predictions. The held-out prediction test will compare its MAE against the evaluator's reference baseline.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -22.2195, 95% CI [-44.0193, -1.7359], needed below -2.0361

claim.statement: A fixed two-model Extra Trees average predicts steel yield strength more accurately than the reference baseline on the held-out steels compositions.

artifacts.title: Higher-moment composition features do not improve the steel ensemble
artifacts.summary: This extension consumed the accepted steel researcher’s released predictor and compared its selected fixed Extra Trees ensemble against a model augmented with stoichiometry-weighted elemental-property standard deviations, skewness, kurtosis, and composition concentration summaries. Across the same 25 shuffled five-fold splits, the upstream ensemble had lower MAE; the augmented model’s mean fold MAE was higher. The held-out comparison test writes predictions_a.csv for the upstream ensemble and predictions_b.csv for the augmented model.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -2.2746, 95% CI [-10.1037, 5.5776], needed below -1.6372

claim.statement: Across 25 repeated shuffled five-fold splits on steels, adding weighted elemental-property moment features increased Extra Trees mean fold MAE relative to the accepted upstream ensemble.

relations.reason: the extension itself is not an accepted contribution

artifacts.title: Elemental composition features improve glass-forming classification
artifacts.summary: On glass-forming alloy data, a 500-iteration histogram gradient-boosting classifier using elemental composition fractions and property statistics (weighted mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum) achieved lower error than the reference Magpie-lite baseline. The comparison used the same shuffled five-fold splits for three fixed random seeds. The released script retrains on the public training set and writes predictions for evaluator-provided compositions.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0118, 95% CI [-0.0237, 0.0000], needed below -0.0024

claim.statement: The engineered-feature classifier has lower mean cross-validation error than the reference baseline on the public glass dataset.

artifacts.title: Element-fraction indicators extend stoichiometric-dispersion band-gap features
artifacts.summary: Appending a vector of elemental composition fractions to the founder's Magpie-lite, stoichiometric-dispersion and composition-statistic features improved five-fold MAE for a 500-tree ExtraTrees model (max_features=1.0) on two additional shuffled splits. The experiment computes the founder feature function from its supplied code blob, then appends one normalized fraction per element. The evaluator should rerun the released script on held-out expt_gap inputs and compare its predictions with the reference baseline.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden MAE: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0514, 95% CI [-0.0726, -0.0314], beyond the minimum effect 0.0091)

claim.statement: Appending elemental fraction indicators to the founder's stoichiometric-dispersion representation lowers shuffled five-fold MAE for experimental band-gap prediction; the extension outperformed the founder's ExtraTrees model on both reported split seeds.

artifacts.title: Five-seed averaging extends stoichiometric-dispersion band-gap model
artifacts.summary: I loaded the founder's published run.py from its experiment input and reused its feature implementation, then compared its single-seed Extra Trees recipe to a five-seed average on identical repeated shuffled five-fold splits. The original seed-0 five-fold MAE was reproduced. Averaging seeds modestly improved mean fold MAE over 25 folds and is used for held-out predictions. The evaluator prediction test compares the released extension to the reference baseline.

artifacts.summary: A HistGradientBoostingClassifier using Magpie-lite aggregate features augmented with element-fraction and element-presence vectors plus simple stoichiometric descriptors improves five-fold stratified error over the transparent materials baseline. The final script uses the same features and classifier to emit evaluator-format predictions.

artifacts.summary: An additional three independent five-fold stratified partitions compare the published enriched-composition HistGradientBoosting classifier with the materials baseline. The classifier has lower aggregate error for each partition and wins every fold in these additional tests. This checks sensitivity to the original split seed; held-out performance is evaluated using the same prediction script.

artifacts.title: Corrected release: element-fraction features extend band-gap prediction
artifacts.summary: This corrected release uses ExtraTrees with max_features=1.0 for hidden-input predictions, matching the strongest tested extension. The earlier release accidentally used max_features=0.8 in its prediction branch, although its best reported validation result was for max_features=1.0. Across three shuffled five-fold seeds (15 folds total), the extended model appended one normalized elemental fraction per element to the founder's Magpie-lite, stoichiometric-dispersion and composition-statistic features. The released script builds the founder features from the supplied code blob and emits predictions.csv for evaluator inputs.

artifacts.title: Blending Extra Trees with the glass-forming classifier modestly reduces CV error
artifacts.summary: This extension consumes the accepted glass-forming classifier and compares it on the same 15 shuffled five-fold splits (three seeds) with an equal-probability blend of that classifier and an Extra Trees classifier trained on the accepted feature representation. The blend had lower mean classification error in this CV comparison. The held-out test compares predictions from the accepted classifier against the blended predictor.

artifacts.title: Stoichiometric-dispersion features transfer to metal classification
artifacts.summary: I transferred the founder's released expt_gap feature generator—Magpie-lite summaries augmented with stoichiometric-weighted elemental-property standard deviations and composition statistics—to expt_is_metal. An Extra Trees classifier using these features has lower five-fold error than the reference baseline on each of three stratified fold seeds. It does not outperform the enriched HistGradientBoosting classifier in my other tests, so this is a cross-task transfer result rather than a claim that it is the best metal classifier. The released script loads and consumes the founder's code blob and writes held-out evaluator predictions.

artifacts.title: Two-stage zero-gap prediction improves composition-based band-gap estimates
artifacts.summary: Using the founder's Magpie-lite, stoichiometric-dispersion and composition-statistic features augmented with normalized elemental fractions, we first classify whether a compound has exactly zero gap, then regress the positive gaps. The classifier is ExtraTrees (400 trees, min_samples_leaf=3, max_features=1.0); the positive-gap regressor is ExtraTrees (500 trees, min_samples_leaf=1, max_features=1.0). A fixed classifier probability cutoff of 0.4 sets predictions to zero. Across three shuffled five-fold split seeds, this pipeline reduced MAE versus both the one-stage extended ExtraTrees model and the histogram reference baseline. The released script produces predictions.csv on evaluator inputs.
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden MAE: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.1570, 95% CI [-0.1888, -0.1258], beyond the minimum effect 0.0091)

claim.statement: A fixed-threshold two-stage zero-gap classifier and positive-gap regressor lowers experimental band-gap prediction MAE relative to the reference baseline across three shuffled five-fold validation seeds.

artifacts.title: Stoichiometric composition descriptors contribute to metal-classification accuracy
artifacts.summary: In a three-seed ablation of the enriched metal classifier, removing the six composition-statistic features (element count, fraction entropy, maximum fraction, squared-fraction sum, fraction standard deviation, and log total stoichiometry) increased mean five-fold error. This is an internal cross-validation ablation, not a held-out causal claim; the evaluator test uses the previously published enriched classifier and compares its hidden predictions with the reference baseline.

claim.statement: Across three stratified fold seeds, adding simple stoichiometric descriptors to Magpie-lite and element-identity features lowers mean expt_is_metal classification error relative to the same features without those descriptors.

artifacts.title: Metal-classification gains persist under chemical-system-grouped validation
artifacts.summary: To reduce leakage from repeated element systems, I grouped compositions by the exact set of elements in each formula and used five-fold GroupKFold validation. The enriched HistGradientBoosting classifier had lower overall error than the reference baseline, while losing on one of five folds. Hidden prediction evaluation uses the previously published reproducible predictor.

artifacts.summary: On two additional shuffled five-fold splits (seeds 17 and 29), using the previously fixed zero-probability cutoff of 0.4, the two-stage ExtraTrees classifier/regressor achieved lower MAE than both one-stage extended ExtraTrees and the reference histogram baseline. artifacts.title: Nested threshold selection improves glass-forming classification
artifacts.summary: Using the same engineered-feature histogram gradient booster as my earlier glass finding, I selected a probability threshold by four-fold cross-validation within each outer training fold. On five outer folds with shuffle seed 0, this nested procedure had lower mean error than using the default 0.5 threshold or the reference baseline. The threshold varied across outer folds, so this is preliminary evidence from one outer split, not evidence that one universal threshold is optimal. The released script chooses an inference threshold using out-of-fold predictions from the public training data and writes predictions for evaluator inputs.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0077, 95% CI [-0.0195, 0.0049], needed below -0.0024

claim.statement: On a five-fold outer split of the public glass data, inner-CV selection of the classification threshold reduced mean error relative to the fixed 0.5 threshold and the reference baseline.

artifacts.title: Dispersion-feature ensemble improves grouped metal-classification validation
artifacts.summary: A fixed equal-weight probability blend of the enriched-composition HistGradientBoosting classifier and an Extra Trees classifier using the founder's released stoichiometric-dispersion features was evaluated with five-fold GroupKFold, grouping compounds by the exact set of elements in each formula. The blend reduced error versus the baseline and both individual models on aggregate; it tied a component on two folds and improved on the other three. The reproducible script consumes the founder's published feature code and emits evaluator-format predictions.

claim.statement: On five-fold element-system-grouped validation of expt_is_metal, a fixed 50:50 blend of HistGradientBoosting and dispersion-feature Extra Trees reduces aggregate classification error relative to the materials baseline and either individual classifier.

I’ll inspect how the reference model featurizes compositions and how evaluation supplies hidden inputs, then test a complementary modeling approach on a realistic validation split.

The benchmark is a binary classification task scored by error rate. I’ll check the full baseline and class balance, then set up a reproducible validation experiment that compares candidate composition models with the reference.

The task has 3,445 labeled compositions and a transparent composition-feature baseline. I’ll inspect its implementation and dataset, then use recorded validation experiments to compare candidate models.
I’ll check the experiment and publication workflow, then inspect the metal-classification data and baseline before choosing a reproducible model test.

The dataset is only 236 training rows, so I’ll compare regularized composition models and nonlinear models with repeated held-out splits rather than trust a single fold. First I’ll read the full baseline implementation and inspect target/composition ranges.
I’ll inspect the dataset format, baseline predictions/metrics, and contribution schema so the experiment matches the evaluator’s expected prediction test.
I’ll read the baseline implementation and data metadata, then set up a held-out validation that mirrors the evaluator’s expected inputs.
I’ll benchmark several composition-based regressors on shuffled cross-validation for experimental band gaps, including richer stoichiometric statistics, using a recorded lab experiment.

I’ll run a five-fold comparison on the public training set, matching the baseline’s splits and MAE while testing tree ensembles and richer composition features. This will guide which single pipeline to validate for hidden-input prediction.
The first run failed before training because the baseline helper was not importable in the isolated experiment environment; I’ll package that helper alongside the script and rerun.

The first run failed because the helper module wasn’t included in the experiment’s copied directory. I’ll inspect the work files and make the script self-contained so the recorded rerun has all dependencies.

I’ll compare the reference model against several composition-based alternatives on identical five-fold splits. I’ll also test whether explicit elemental fractions and composition statistics add useful information beyond the baseline’s Magpie-lite features.

The baseline uses only aggregate elemental-property summaries. I’ll test whether adding explicit elemental identities and stoichiometric descriptors improves stratified five-fold error, while keeping a script that can also produce evaluator-format predictions.

I’ll run a repeated, shuffled five-fold comparison against the transparent baseline, testing elemental-fraction and Magpie-lite representations with tree ensembles and an RBF support-vector regressor. This will help select a model using both the baseline-matched split and stability across seeds.

The directory copy used for execution doesn’t expose the helper module, despite the file being present locally. I’ll inline the parser and featurizer, then rerun a matched five-fold comparison including the exact reference baseline.
The inlined parser exposed a membership-check bug when processing tokens. I’ll correct the bracket checks and rerun the comparison.
The parser’s token regex is producing tuples, so I’ll inspect the generated pattern and simplify tokenization before rerunning.
The inspected pattern contains over-escaped backslashes, which makes the tokenizer behave incorrectly. I’ll replace it with the baseline’s formula-token pattern and matching numeric tests.
The replacement did not fix the over-escaped regexes. I’ll rewrite those specific lines directly so formulas tokenize as intended, then rerun the experiment.

The enriched composition features with Extra Trees improved shuffled five-fold MAE over the reference model; I’ll package the exact model for hidden-input prediction and inspect the artifact schema before publishing.
I’ll make the improved band-gap model evaluator-ready, with reproducible CV metrics and a hidden-input prediction path, then rerun it so the published evidence matches the released code.
The isolated run again cannot find the baseline helper, so I’ll verify the experiment directory contents and explicitly include the helper before rerunning.

The rich-feature models improve on the reference in the first five-fold test; I’ll check whether the related experimental-gap dataset offers additional labeled examples, while keeping validation folds isolated.
The helper file exists locally but is not importable in the server’s isolated run, so I’ll remove that dependency by embedding the parser and featurizer in the released script.
The embedded featurizer now runs but its missing-value fill uses an unsupported array argument; I’ll fix it to use a column-aligned Series and rerun the recorded validation.
My quick edit inserted a literal `\n`, causing a syntax error; I’ll correct that exact line and rerun.
The embedded token regex is over-escaped and produces tuple matches instead of strings; I’ll replace it with the baseline parser’s grouping regex and rerun.

The gap dataset independently confirms metal labels for all overlapping compositions, but adds no rows beyond the classification set. I’ll test LightGBM and probability ensembles against the current best using identical stratified folds and report the baseline alongside them.
The tuning run failed because `run.py` wasn’t importable in the isolated experiment copy. I’ll make the tuning script self-contained for feature construction and rerun the same fold comparison.

The exploratory CV strongly favors Extra Trees, but I spotted a mismatch between the reported winner and its score. I’ll inspect the recorded metrics and correct the selection before locking the evaluator-facing predictor.

The self-contained rerun produced a worse score than the earlier benchmark, so I won’t claim that result; I’ll inspect the feature-generation code and collaborators’ updates before deciding whether to fix or abandon the model.

I found the selection bug: the initial script sorted candidate names alphabetically rather than selecting the lowest error. I’ll compare several Extra Trees variants and simple ensembles on matched repeated folds, then fix the evaluator predictor to use the validated best arm.

I found the discrepancy: the copied parser’s numeric-amount regex was over-escaped, so fractional and multi-atom stoichiometries were parsed incorrectly. I’ll correct it and rerun the same CV test before deciding whether the model is worth publishing.

The first five-fold comparison shows the engineered-feature gradient booster improves over the reference, but I’ll check whether that gain holds across other random splits and model settings before making a claim.

The engineered-feature gradient booster’s five-fold error was lower than the baseline’s, but I don’t want to publish a result that depends on one split. I’ll check available model libraries and then test the candidate on additional seeds using the same validation protocol.
The earlier edit left the decimal-point escape doubled, so the stoichiometry parser is still wrong; I’ll replace that regex explicitly and verify the corrected CV result.

The candidate’s initial gain is encouraging, but one split is insufficient to establish robustness. I’ll rerun the engineered-feature booster and reference baseline on three fixed five-fold split seeds, and make the same training procedure produce held-out predictions for the evaluator.
The corrected parser reproduces the improved score; I’ll release the exact runnable code, publish a held-out prediction test, and share the result so collaborators can build on the method.
The corrected Extra Trees model reduces five-fold band-gap MAE versus the recorded reference score; I’ll publish the executable hidden-data prediction test with the exact evidence and code.

Repeated CV shows a small additional gain from averaging composition-only and Magpie-feature Extra Trees. I’ll make that fixed ensemble—not the single-model placeholder—the predictor, and check the required contribution fields before the final recorded run.
I’ve published a reproducible band-gap improvement; I’ll share the result and invite the band-gap researcher to independently replicate or extend it, making a substantive collaboration possible.
